checks: The interior source makes each cut proper with positive section measure. A facet through P_j has zero flux for x-P_j, and the opposite facet has constant full flux d times the simplex volume.

The cap's outward cut normal is the negative normalized v_i. Its flux density is t_ij divided by the normal length, giving Q_i=F_ij+t_ij S_i/d. Intersections with old facets have zero surface measure, including cuts through some vertices. In d=1 the cut point is distinct from both endpoints.
Division by S_i M and the zero sum of the normals give unit column sums. Taking the barycentric mean in each row gives a_i and rearranging gives both t_ij and the normalized row quantity.
Source 63504696488203c3 §1 uses the same shared physical facets and arbitrary proper cap incidences.

overlap.comparison: Computes weighted full-facet payment for vertex-isolating cuts with prescribed own section centroids. Here rows may capture several vertices, and the identity determines every individual face fraction before any weighted payment.
Starts from an abstract nonnegative column-stochastic matrix and optimizes its row capacities. It does not represent the entries by actual captured facet fractions.

readability: The definitions, scope, and proof order are clear.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The facet flux identity holds for every proper through-source row and yields the claimed physical column-stochastic matrix.
